_meta.description: Per-provider unit prices in USD — editable config. Estimates and spend math read this file; no price is hardcoded (BUILD_PLAN 1.6, §0, risks #1/#5).

units.tts: usd_per_1k_chars — price per 1,000 characters; estimates ceil to whole units
units.video: usd_per_second — price per second of clip; estimates ceil fractional seconds up

_meta.warning: Research spikes 2.0/4.0 (2026-11-06) verified the model IDs and prices below against Google's official docs — see research/gemini-api.md and research/gemini-video.md for every derivation and citation. The gemini 'verified' flag is true since task 2.3 wired the real TTS provider (the placeholder era ended with the spike; test_cost.py pins the spike-verified models/prices).
recheck: 2026-12-01: Gemini 2.5 family auto-routing begins; 2.5 TTS deprecation flow — do not add 2.5 models back.
2026-12-03: gemini-omni-1.1-flash requests auto-route to gemini-omni-1.2-flash and bill at 1.2 rates (spike 4.0 §1) — the video row already uses 1.2; re-verify $12.00/1M output video tokens held.
2027-01-01: gemini-3.8-flash-tts / flash-lite-tts audio prices double ($9->$18, $6->$12 per 1M audio tokens) — re-derive tts price.

TTS billing is per OUTPUT audio token (25 tokens/s); the per-1k-chars figure assumes English at 120 wpm (11.4 chars/s, conservative vs ~150 wpm mid-rate). ffprobe durations at task 2.4 reconcile actual spend.

video price covers 720p (5,792 output tokens/s x $12.00/1M = $0.069504/s, rounded up). The provider always requests 720p and assembly upscales to platform dims (spike 4.0 §7.5); native 1080p would bill $0.104/s (8,688 tok/s) — moving the resolution means moving this row and the provider's DEFAULT_RESOLUTION together.

gemini.label: Google Gemini API (AI Studio key) — BUILD_PLAN §0 recommendation
gemini.note: Prices and model IDs verified 2026-11-06 by research spike 2.0 (research/gemini-api.md). TTS has a free tier; image and video require a paid (billing-enabled) project — fresh keys sit in Tier 1 with a $10-per-10-min Google-side spend limiter, so expect 429s below the app's own cap.

tts.note: Billed per output audio token (25 tokens/s, $9.00/1M through 2026-12-31, $18.00 from 2027-01-01; free tier exists). $0.02/1k chars = conservative 120 wpm English (~2,193 audio tokens per 1k chars; mid-rate 150 wpm gives ~$0.016). Cheaper alternative: gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts ($6.00/1M audio => ~0.014 conservative, $0.0015 per 10s). Legacy gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts still listed but deprecated — do not use.

image.note: Page-stated 2K equivalent ($30.00/1M image tokens x 1,680 tokens); 2K chosen because platforms.json targets 1080px-class dims that 1K cannot cover (9:16@1K is 768x1376) — generate 2K, downscale in assembly. 1K = $0.0336, 4K = $0.113. Alternatives: gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image 1K-only $0.0336; gemini-3.1-flash-image $0.067 (1K)–$0.151 (4K); gemini-3-pro-image $0.134–$0.24. Paid only (no free tier). Imagen shut down; gemini-2.5-flash-image deprecated, shuts down 2027-03-15.

video.note: Spike 4.0 (research/gemini-video.md, 2026-11-06): standard tier $12.00/1M output video tokens at 5,792 tokens per second of 720p video = $0.069504/s (pricing page: 'approximately $0.07 per second, ~$0.70 for a 10s clip'), rounded up; input tokens $1.50/1M are negligible per clip. Paid only (no free tier). The provider always requests 720p and assembly upscales to platform dims — the docs mark 1080p/4k '(upscaled)', i.e. the API itself renders 720p and upscales, so local upscaling is the ~33%-cheaper default; native 1080p would bill $0.104/s (8,688 tok/s), 360p $0.023/s, 4K $0.209/s. Clips render 3-15s at 24 FPS; beats outside that window are rejected before spend (video.py guards). Veo 3.1 Preview was shut down 2026-10-22; gemini-omni-1.1-flash ($17.50/1M = $0.1014/s) auto-routes to 1.2 billing from 2026-12-03.
